analysis.title: The breakdown but where is the panic
key_insights: SPX is breaking below the major trendline, the 200-day moving average and the trading range in place since May. 7200 is the short-term line in the sand, and a close below it could open the door to more aggressive selling.
SPX is down 1.4% while VIX approaches 30, which The Market Ear calls excessive for a move of that size unless the market is pricing something worse ahead. Volatility is showing early signs of panic.

Nomura's McElligott sees the ingredients for a mechanical relief rally once this week's major risk events clear. A volatility reset could force dealer buying and systematic strategies may add exposure. The Market Ear notes everyone expects the same squeeze, and a failure to rally despite supportive flows would be a more troubling signal.
TS Lombard warns next year's US EPS growth could disappoint because of building wage pressures, rising rates and capex growth that may be peaking.
TS Lombard argues sticky services inflation and a reaccelerating labour market could force the Fed to hike more aggressively than markets expect.

BTIG notes that on November 17 AAPL closed 1.2% below its 52-week high while SPX traded below its 200-day moving average. This combination has occurred on only 14 trading days in 20 years, clustered in 2007, 2010 and 2011.
GS's early-November snapshot has Apple at about 35x forward earnings versus 19x for NDX. On FCF yield Apple is slightly above NDX, with the relative spread broadly in line with historical trends.

The Market Ear is increasingly tempted to reverse its Sep 23 long Apple/short NVDA trade, particularly for those who took the original setup, since the relative move has been large with Apple holding up and the AI complex hit hard.
EEM has become a large Asia AI bet, but the commodity link remains. With tech and commodities both under pressure, the space has been hit from all sides.
EEM weekly RSI is at its lowest level since November 2022. Previous sharp pullbacks, including from RSI readings above the current level, were followed by powerful reversals higher.

GS data show fundamental long/short funds cutting exposure. Gross leverage is down 4.4 points in November to 206.3% (23rd percentile over the past year). Net leverage is down 7.6 points to 41.6%, the lowest in five years.
GS data show hedge funds selling global tech at the fastest trailing six-week pace in a decade (z-score -4.4). The global tech long/short ratio fell from a YTD peak of 2.9 to 1.79, near 10-year lows.
